items.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I worked in one at back of Roosevelt called Seymour’s, which was... Seymour Schwarz had a record shop... He’d do Dixieland... and I’d have all the modern guys up there.

ctx.x: And so you saw an opportunity here to expand it, extend it beyond a listening club here.

Well I didn’t actually look at it that way, it just came about. Like we say “like topsy” it just happened. People would hear these groups and they’d say, “Say, can you get this group for our fraternity dance or something?” And I’d say “sure,” you know. And that happened and then somebody came to me and said, “Would you like to work on weekends at the Bee Hive in Hyde Park as the host?” “Sure.” “And do Monday night sessions?” “Sure.” I was tryin’ to earn money of course to raise my family, so I did that. I worked…
Wait, wait, wait. Go back. So Sonny Rollins playing an alto.
